scope.direct: New optimizers, algorithmic variants, and substantively new optimizer/scheduler/state-management wrappers; includes theoretical and specialized algorithms, with scope and costs stated in summaries.
scope.weak: Substantive Muon theory, mechanisms, benchmarks, and implementation research without a newly proposed optimizer.
scope.resources: Muon technical explanations, implementations, and experimental resources.
scope.excluded: Physical muons; ordinary reuse of existing non-Muon optimizers; pure non-Muon analyses without new algorithm design; unrelated combinatorial/metaheuristic applications.

method: Re-read all current CSVs and README at a pinned live main commit; preserve every existing row and prior known duplicate exception.

Audit each calendar segment, not just the latest week. Extend the prior cs.LG-focused search through math.OC, math.NA, cs.NE and stat.ML native listings, exact-month searches, primary publication histories and original technical resources.

Title screens are discovery only. Retained papers were checked in full-text algorithm, assumption, experiment and limitation sections; original arXiv submission dates were retained despite later revisions or printed manuscript dates.
Deduplicate canonical arXiv/URL identity and normalized title across direct, weak and resource tables. Distinguish new update designs and substantive wrappers from pure analysis or ordinary reuse.
Inspect substantive paper-/author-linked code before setting code URLs. README-only placeholders, inaccessible repositories and unverified implementations receive blank code fields.

Resolve all six explicitly recorded unreviewed title leads before publication: five additional designs retained, one withdrawn paper rejected. IAdam remains pending because primary full text is inaccessible.

Validate every CSV cell through independent artifact-tool import, preserve canonical CSV round trips, and verify README renders all rows. Publish with an expected-head lease and read back every committed file.
